hook.name: hook
hook.reason: Alexander's cold demand to 'Read the names' immediately sets up a public confrontation and shaming.

narrative_tension.name: narrative_tension
narrative_tension.reason: Tension steadily escalates from the public reading of names to the exposure of treason, panic, and an attempted escape that gets blocked.

cliffhanger.name: cliffhanger
cliffhanger.reason: The cut lands squarely on the trapped villain's terrified face as his escape is intercepted, leaving his immediate reckoning hanging.
cliffhanger.open_question: How will Lord Sterling escape or face justice now that his exit is blocked?

context_independence.name: context_independence
context_independence.reason: The core conflict—a wronged, presumed-dead man returning to expose corrupt nobles who stole his life—is easy to grasp without prior episodes.
context_independence.blind_summary: A presumed-dead lord named Alexander returns to a cathedral to publicly expose the nobles who betrayed him and stole his title. As his conspirators panic and try to flee, they find all escape routes blocked by the authorities.

confusions.issue: Exact pre-existing relationships and military betrayal details are implied but not fully explained.

curiosity_gap.name: curiosity_gap
curiosity_gap.reason: The clip delivers a satisfying sequence of public exposure while leaving the ultimate reckoning and fallout open.
revealed: Rupert and Lord Sterling conspired against him and took his title
The conspiracy is being publicly laid bare
withheld: What specific punishment Alexander will inflict

emotional_impact.name: emotional_impact
emotional_impact.reason: Watching corrupt conspirators squirm and panic as their crimes are exposed creates a strong sense of poetic justice.

stakes.value: A betrayed noble returns from the dead to reclaim his stolen title and exact vengeance on the conspirators.
